knowledge_cards.claim: SpanSynth bounds replacement to a region but does not waveform-preserve unchanged notes inside it.
The 25 Hz latent grid expands edit boundaries to 40 ms multiples; requested and applied intervals must be recorded separately.
Sample-exact preservation outside a hard splice does not prove click-free or gain-continuous boundaries.
Released mono inference cannot preserve stereo pan, width or interchannel phase without a separate strategy and test.
Generated-note metrics need evaluator and codec ceilings because both dominate part of the observed score loss.
FlowEdit trades some similarity scores against quality and note-add/delete behavior; it is not a monotonic upgrade.
Insensitivity to 1-5 ms MIDI shifts leaves precise timing control unverified.
Unrecorded random state and mutable model revision prevent exact replay of public SpanSynth runs.
MambaVoice is perceptually comparable, not superior, to VoViT in the reported small test.
MambaVoice network forward time excludes facial preprocessing and buffering and is not end-to-end latency.
Audiovisual identity grounding still requires leakage, additivity, silence, phase, peak and edit tests before pseudo-stem use.
A linked repository returning 404 blocks reproduction despite the paper's code-availability statement.

handoff: Treat SpanSynth as a mono generative research editor, not a transparent repair tool: null-test identical MIDI inside the region, record 40 ms-expanded bounds, pin checkpoint and seed, and test seams and peaks before listening. Treat MambaVoice as a pseudo-stem candidate only after artifacts reappear; current evidence supports comparability to VoViT, not safe mix editing.
